ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a current source, labeled Is = 3∠30° A, with the direction upward; the upper end of the current source passes through a 5 Ω resistor to reach the upper node of the right-side network. This right-side network has two parallel branches: the middle branch is a j4 Ω reactance in series with a 3 Ω resistor, so the impedance is 3 + j4 Ω; the right branch is a capacitive reactance -j4 Ω. The lower common node returns to the lower end of the current source. Reasoning: First find the equivalent impedance of the parallel part. Let Z1 = 3 + j4 Ω, Z2 = -j4 Ω, then Zp = Z1 Z2 / (Z1 + Z2) = ((3 + j4)(-j4)) / ((3 + j4) + (-j4)) = (16 - j12) / 3 = 16/3 - j4 Ω. The total impedance is 5 Ω in series with this parallel equivalent impedance, so Z_total = 5 + (16/3 - j4) = 31/3 - j4 Ω, whose imaginary part Im(Z_total) = -4 Ω. The magnitude of the current source current is |3∠30°| = 3 A, therefore reactive power Q = |I|^2 Im(Z_total) = 3^2 × (-4) = -36 Var.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Uses a direct equivalent-impedance reduction of the entire circuit, rather than solving individual node voltages or branch powers.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the diagram as a 3∠30° A current source feeding a 5 Ω series resistor, then a parallel network between the top and bottom nodes: one branch is j4 Ω in series with 3 Ω, and the other branch is a capacitor of impedance -j4 Ω.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to determine that the requested quantity is the reactive power Q in Var.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply series/parallel impedance reduction: Z_mid = 3 + j4, Z_cap = -j4, so Z_parallel = (Z_mid || Z_cap). The 5 Ω resistor is then added in series. Reactive power for the whole circuit/load is Q = |I|^2 Im(Z_total); the current phase is irrelevant because only |I| is used. This gives Im(Z_total) = -4 Ω and Q = 3^2(-4) = -36 Var.
